join_order.notes: Drive from mi via movie_info__info_type_id CSR; expected ~few hundred thousand mi rows for it1_id
After substring filters, lookup production_year by movie_id (dense PK)
Resolve us_code at runtime; check cn_cc[company_id-1]==us_code for each mc row in [off[mv], off[mv+1])
Existence: off[mv+1] > off[mv]; keyword and company_type joins are existence-only against dense PKs and implicitly satisfied

data_structures.cn_country_code_array: int16[234997] mmap (dense PK; direct index by id-1)
data_structures.us_code_scalar: int16 (resolved at runtime from cn dict)
data_structures.mi_info_varlen: int64 offsets + char dat (memmem for substring)
data_structures.min_mi_info: string_view tracker (lex min of varlen bytes)
data_structures.min_t_title: string_view tracker (lex min of varlen bytes)

parallelism.notes: Parallelize over [lo,hi) range of mi_it_row[] for it1_id; each thread maintains local MIN string_views, reduce at end with mutex/atomic_min

implementation_notes: Resolve us_code by scanning company_name dict for '[us]'; resolve it1_id by scanning info_type for 'release dates'.

Order of per-row predicates inside the CSR loop: (1) mi_note_match (cheapest indicative substring), (2) mi_info_match (USA prefix + memmem), (3) production_year check, (4) mc semi-join with cn country_code, (5) at1 existence, (6) mk existence.
ct and k joins reduce to existence against dense PKs and are satisfied implicitly by mc.company_type_id and mk.keyword_id being valid foreign keys; no explicit probe needed.
MIN over varlen: keep best (offset, length) pair per thread; final reduction picks lex-smallest byte sequence.
